element.description: Use this wording for element-of-leverage pages where completion means a merged agent-authored PR.

jobToBeDone.title: Complete a Coding Task by Delegating to an Asynchronous Agent
jobToBeDone.body: Developers assign issues to a coding agent, which creates pull requests that humans review, guide, and merge.

whatCountsAsCompletion.title: A Copilot-authored PR that gets merged
whatCountsAsCompletion.body: Valid = PR was reviewed and merged by a human. Failed/flawed = PR closed without merging.

jobClass.title: Value-creating
jobClass.body: Valid completions create valuable work product.

efficiency.description: Use this wording for efficiency pages where the questions are: at the population level, how many completions are occurring and how many dev-hours are being consumed; and at the individual level, how many completions each active user generates per hour spent.

jobToBeDone.title: Complete a Coding Task by Delegating to an Asynchronous Agent
jobToBeDone.body: Developers delegate implementation work to the coding agent, which creates pull requests that humans review, guide, and merge.

whatCountsAsCompletion.title: A Copilot-authored PR that gets merged
whatCountsAsCompletion.body: Valid = PR was reviewed and merged by a human. Failed/flawed = PR closed without merging.

jobClass.title: Value-creating
jobClass.body: Valid completions create valuable work product.

howEfficiencyImproves.title: Developers use GitHub Agents to complete additional Coding tasks, and/or reduce hours spent or other costs.
howEfficiencyImproves.body:
Efficiency can show up if a completion 
1) consumes fewer dev-hours, 
2) encounters less risk, 
3) is increasing in session duration, scope, or difficulty.

estimatesAndAssumptions.title: Completion counts and hours spent per completion are modeled from agent session activity
estimatesAndAssumptions.body:
Hours invested per completion is estimated from agent session duration and level of human intervention. 
Completion counts are drawn from merged Copilot-authored PRs.

indicatorsOfProgress.title: Rising completions per user and falling hours per completion indicate that agent delegation is becoming more efficient.
indicatorsOfProgress.body:
Completion rate, completions per active user, and hours invested per completion are the primary indicators. 
When these indicators move together in the expected direction, we have higher confidence that efficiency is genuinely improving.
